paragraphs: Here's what I love about this song, friend: David doesn't clean it up before he brings it to God. He says rejected, broken, angry, and he says it right to God's face (Psalm 60:1). Then, in the very same breath, he says "restore us!" That tells me the honest prayer and the hopeful prayer can live in the same sentence, and God can handle both.

Notice what happens in the middle. God speaks from His sanctuary, and He opens with "I will triumph!" (Psalm 60:6). Gilead is His, Manasseh is His, Ephraim is His helmet, Judah is His scepter (Psalm 60:7). Nothing about the trouble got smaller, but the One holding all of it got a whole lot clearer, and THAT is the turn in this song.

So when David lands on "the help of man is worthless," he isn't being gloomy (Psalm 60:11). He's being smart, because he knows where the real help lives. "With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies" (Psalm 60:12). Next time your day shakes you, baker, say it all out loud to God, then walk back into that fight with Him beside you.
